Wellington: A Documentary Film: The Phenomenon of Healing
Bruno Groening's legacy continues to inspire people today through the ongoing activities of the Bruno Groening Circle of Friends.

About this Event



Documentary Film: The Phenomenon of Healing

In the 1950s, Bruno Groening gained international attention as a spiritual figure whose words and presence left a profound impression on thousands. When he passed away in 1959, many thought the movement around him would come to an end — but instead, it continued to grow.

The Phenomenon of Healing is a powerful documentary that follows the journey of the Bruno Groening Circle of Friends, a global community that carries on his Teaching to this day. Through compelling personal interviews, rare archival footage and commentary from healthcare professionals, this three-part documentary film shows how Bruno Groening's legacy continues to inspire people today - regardless of faith, belief, nationality or culture. Through this, many have experienced emotional and physical well-being, as well as a renewed sense of purpose in their lives.

Whether you're curious about spirituality, exploring personal growth, or interested in the historical context of healing traditions, this film offers a fresh and engaging perspective. Everyone is welcome to attend.

Admission is free – voluntary donations are appreciated.

When: Saturday 3 October 2026

Time: 1:00pm to 7:00pm (Includes 2 breaks)

Where: Quaker Hall, 7 Moncrieff Street, Mt Victoria, Wellington

Contact: Anouk - 0210627762 |

More information about the film: www.bruno-groening-film.org

Visit our website: www.bruno-groening.org/en

---------------------------

Please note: This film and event are intended for informational purposes only. The personal experiences shared in the film reflect the views and stories of individuals and do not constitute medical advice. No diagnosis, treatment, or healing outcomes are offered or guaranteed. Always seek guidance from a qualified healthcare professional for medical concerns.

Reel Rock 20 brings a new collection of films celebrating ambition, resilience and the relentless pursuit of the impossible.

About this Event



Reel Rock 20 brings the world’s greatest climbing stories back to the big screen with a thrilling new collection of films celebrating ambition, resilience and the relentless pursuit of the impossible.

This year’s program follows four extraordinary climbing journeys: Olympic champion Janja Garnbret sets her sights on Bibiliographie; Michaela Kiersch’s historic quest to achieve the ultimate climbing double of 5.15 and V15; Colin Haley’s legendary winter solo push on Cerro Torre; and Ben Mayforth’s determined pursuit of 5.13 as he continues to redefine what is possible in adaptive climbing.

JANJA GARNBRET
Olympic champion Janja Garnbret sets her sights on the legendary climb Bibiographie
Featuring: Janja Garnbret

MICHAELA KIERSCH
Michaela Kiersch sets out to make climbing history by becoming the first woman to complete the ultimate climbing double: sending both 5.15 and V15.

Her pursuit demands extraordinary strength, precision and perseverance as she pushes the limits of performance across two of climbing’s most difficult disciplines.
Featuring: Michaela Kiersch

COLIN HALEY
Elite alpinist Colin Haley lays everything on the line in a legendary winter solo push on Cerro Torre - one of Patagonia’s most iconic and unforgiving peaks.
Alone in extreme conditions, Haley takes on a bold alpine challenge where speed, commitment and survival are inseparable.
Featuring: Colin Haley

BEN MAYFORTH
Ben Mayforth redefines adaptive climbing through an intense and resolute pursuit of 5.13.
Driven by determination and an uncompromising approach to progression, Mayforth challenges expectations and expands the possibilities of adaptive climbing.
Featuring: Ben Mayforth

Tickets are on sale now at reelrockfilmtour.com.

long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in B&W (Public Talk-John Walsh, Patrick Reynolds, Andrew Barrie)
Architecture writer John Walsh and photographer Patrick Reynolds discuss their city walking guides and the heritage places they reveal, bringing together Walsh’s deep knowledge of Aotearoa New Zealand architecture and Reynolds’ distinctive photographic eye.

About the speakers
John Walsh is a leading New Zealand architecture writer. He edited Architecture New Zealand magazine for a decade, and has written numerous books on New Zealand architecture, among them the newly revised Auckland Architecture: A Walking Guide, which features photographs by Patrick Reynolds.

Patrick Reynolds is probably best known for his exceptional architectural and interior photographs that appear in publications such as Urbis and Vogue Living. However, over the past 20 years he has developed a highly successful parallel career as a leading photographer within New Zealand contemporary visual arts. As an exhibiting artist his work is about New Zealand landscape, nature, architecture, patterns of seeing, and – just as importantly – about the art and place of photography.

Professor Andrew Barrie
New Zealand-born architectural critic and designer, Prof. Andrew Barrie discusses the research and publication of Block maps, drawing on his work as an architectural critic, designer, author, and educator with deep connections to architecture in Japan and Aotearoa New Zealand.

About the speaker
Professor Andrew Barrie is a New Zealand-born architectural critic and designer formerly based in Tokyo. After completing doctoral studies in Japan, Andrew was a project architect in the office of Toyo Ito, one of the world’s most innovative and influential architects, and later at Cheshire Architects in Auckland. Andrew own design work is widely celebrated, having won numerous awards in both Japan and NZ, including a prestigious named award from the New Zealand Institute of Architects—and has been exhibited nationally and internationally. He is a regular contributor to architecture and design journals and has authored three books on the work of Japanese architects. He has made significant contributions to architectural culture in New Zealand, recognized by the award (with the Block Foundation) of the NZIA’s Auckland Cup for services to architecture, and his election to the Royal Society of New Zealand.

BELTANE SONG & SOUND CEREMONY
Beltane Sound & Voice Ceremony

Sing, Sound and Meditate — Friday 30 October, Paraparaumu

Beltane, the ancient Celtic festival marking the start of summer, is a threshold of fertility, creation and abundance. The earth is bursting into life, and so are we.

You are warmly invited to gather with me in a ceremonial circle to celebrate this turning of the wheel. Together we'll tune into the sacred energies and possibilities of this time, opening ourselves to balance, nourishment, new growth and positive change.

Part one: Voice and Spirit

We begin by calling in the supportive presence of Spirit, the ancestors, the forces of Nature and our highest Selves. The land and the unseen realms have always been at the heart of my practice, and they will hold us throughout.

From there I'll guide you through meditation, gentle Qigong, and conscious sounding and toning to balance and align your energy system. We'll sing beautiful healing chants from many traditions, and play with guided vocal improvisation for freedom, upliftment and joy.

There's something quietly powerful about co-creating a sacred group sound. It lifts us, supports us in releasing what we no longer need, and makes space for new visions to take root. We'll honour that with journaling prompts inspired by Beltane and a moment of intention setting for the season ahead.

Part two: Sound Healing

The second half is a dedicated sound bath. You'll lie back and simply receive, letting the sound carry you into deep relaxation, stillness and peace, with the gratitude that often arrives in that stillness.

Conscious voice work and sound healing can support us physically, mentally, emotionally, energetically and spiritually, and a growing body of research backs up what so many of us feel. I'm happy to share more about these benefits if you'd like to read further.

All are welcome

You might not think you can sing and sound. Come and find out. No experience or preparation is needed, just your willingness to gather.

Donna van Talgon (aka. Matt Middleton of Crude fame describes their music as a "Watersian descent into the mind of madness, chronozone. Utter postmodernism, samples from multifarious eras and ethnicities and qualities gratuitously reworked on-a-whim, a mixture of pure noise and cuts of electronic, a juggernaut, a plunderphonic ride into irregularity, dissonance, discord, deconstruction, re-absorption, loops."

Indigogue Browne is a multidisciplinary artist and filmmaker producing chaotic semi-improvised sparkly harsh noise-pop and omnichord meanderings.

Pyramid Club is excited to present Japanese musician, performance and visual artist Kina:suttsu. Utilising saxophone, electronics, noise, and field recordings, Kina:suttsu creates immersive performances that blur the boundaries between ancient ritual and contemporary experimental music.

Since releasing her first album in 2005, she has performed and exhibited in Japan and internationally. Her releases include music on labels in the UK and France, including a cassette as NAVU and a collaborative release with Phil MFU, Zongamin, E-Da (ex Boredoms, Seefeel). She has recorded with legendary bassist Jah Wobble and released a live recording with Damo Suzuki. In 2021, she appeared in and composed the soundtrack for British filmmaker Daisy Dickinson’s short film Kaki no Shizuku, which was selected for the Los Angeles Film Awards.

This is music as a living system - a real-time collaboration where non-human organisms shape the sonic outcome alongside human performers.

F*ck the Small Talk: Wellington #7 🌈
🎟️ Sign up here: https://luma.com/ftst7wellington 🎟️

F*ck the Small Talk has traveled the world from Berlin, Melbourne, London, Lisbon, and Mexico City, to Lisbon and is now coming to Wellington! 🇳🇿


📦 WHAT'S THIS ABOUT?

FTST is a one-of-a-kind social experience where strangers come together for an afternoon of meaningful, fun, and deep conversation. It’s also just a different & cool way of meeting new people by getting a bit out of your comfort zone and skipping the small talk!

Join us for games, talks, and connections with friends you haven’t met yet. Join if you get annoyed after being asked what you do, where you are from, and how long you have been in Wellington every single time you meet someone. If you feel that there are better questions in life then this is the place for you. 🙌


🎈 HOW DOES IT WORK?

We start with a short & sweet intro talk followed by a few light-hearted group games to warm up. Don't worry, nothing too awkward! After that, we split you up into small groups and start with the conversation rounds (with 3-4 people). We'll have awesome question cards that will guide the flow of the conversation. You’ll never have to speak in public if you don’t want to!


🕹 HOW TO JOIN?

Take 2 minutes to fill out our form 👇🏼
https://luma.com/ftst7wellington

Our events are limited to 30 handpicked guests to ensure a cozy atmosphere. We prioritize a balance in gender and cultural diversity, making each gathering a unique blend of perspectives! If you're invited you'll receive an invite with a special link via our ticketing platform Luma :)


🧧 HOW MUCH IS IT?

The cost to attend is NZD 23-28 and includes the following:

⏰ 3 hours of facilitated and curated activities
🥪 Light snacks to keep the energy going (only if outdoors)
👥 A space to meet new people in the least boring way possible
💛 Supporting our mission to slowly eliminate small talk around the world
🎫 Also includes those pesky ticket fees!


🌳 WHERE IS IT?

We host our events in awesome cafes, rooftops, and bars across the city. We only reveal the location to ticket holders 24 hours before the event.


💛 WHAT THEY SAY

🗣 “Great way to connect with people in a more meaningful way. Get to the heart of the matter, dive straight into what really counts!” - Matthias


🗣 “This is the kind of activity humanity needs every weekend. Thank you for all.” - Sonya


🗣 “F*ck the Small Talk changes the narrative from "Where are you from?" to "When was the last time you laughed uncontrollably?" and I think that's beautiful.” - Monika


🗣 “I loved F*ck the small talk, I was a little bit nervous at first but they are pros at making you feel comfortable with the rest of the group, the activities are really fun and I enjoyed every second (consider that the one who's saying this is very, very shy). Give it a try!” - Brenda


🗣 "it’s a wonderful experience, it’s like being a kid again, when you were at the park, playing with other kids, and just decided you were going to be best friends for the next hours. Maybe you’ll never see those kids again. But that hour was amazing because you both opened up and trusted each other." - Sara


🗣 “Lively, interesting, introspective, completely open and no judgement. Everyone that joined was ready for great conversation and helped with different perspectives. So much fun! I can't wait for the next one! “ - Yaz


Check out our 100+ Google reviews: https://goo.gl/maps/TpZy77bfPFkGoikn7 🫶


🤓 FAQ

• Can I come alone?
Of course, in fact, we encourage it! 99% of people do.


• I signed up but never got an invite. Why?
We usually get a high volume of sign-ups yet we like to keep it cozy & only about 30 people. We believe this is a good number to ensure an awesome experience! Please try again next time if do not receive an invite - no hard feelings 💛


• Why do you charge?
We value our time and put a lot of love, planning, and effort into creating & designing these experiences. ♥️ This is our project/business and what we give to the world and we think everything should be a fair exchange! However, money should never be the reason for people not to attend. If you can’t afford it simply get in touch with us :)


• I'm digging this! Can I get involved somehow?
Sure thing, send us a message!


• Can I bring my cute dog/llama?
It depends on where the event is! Message us to make sure. But it's always a YES in our hearts.


• Can I get a refund if I can't make it?
Unfortunately, we do not offer refunds or ticket transfers to another event date if you cannot attend with a notice of less than 5 days notice. BUTTTT feel free to pass on your ticket to a friend, provided they also sign up for the form :)
